## 🎨 Design
- **ASCII init-log banner.** The container now prints the Junker-der-Provinz banner at startup, matching the other repos in the family.

## 🐛 Fixed
- **Overrides are now actually loaded, switching Synapse from SQLite to Postgres.** Earlier builds wrote an `include_config_files:` directive into `homeserver.yaml` to pull in `homeserver-overrides.yaml`, but **Synapse has no such directive**: it silently ignored the include, so the overrides (Postgres, federation, TURN, registration, presence, retention) were never applied and Synapse ran on a local **SQLite** database at `/data/homeserver.db` instead of your configured Postgres. `homeserver-overrides.yaml` is now passed to Synapse as a second `--config-path` in the synapse service (Synapse's `--config-path` is repeatable and merges in order, the documented pattern), the bogus `include_config_files:` block is no longer written, and the stale block is stripped from existing `homeserver.yaml` on upgrade. (Thanks to **@paulmeier**, issue #3 / PR #4.)
- **Repaired the release workflow** (`release.yml`) that was malformed and broke CI linting on `main`.
- **Breaking, read before updating.** On first start after updating, Synapse will load the overrides and switch to **Postgres**, which is empty unless you migrate. Your existing rooms, users and history live in `/data/homeserver.db` and become unreachable until you port them. Before relying on the update, choose one: **keep your data** by porting SQLite to Postgres with [`synapse_port_db`](https://element-hq.github.io/synapse/latest/postgres.html#porting-from-sqlite) then start the updated container; or **start fresh on Postgres** by renaming the old DB so it can't be picked up and letting Synapse create a clean schema (`docker exec Matrix mv /data/homeserver.db /data/homeserver.db.old`). The init script now prints a loud warning at startup whenever a legacy `/data/homeserver.db` is present, so you won't miss this.
- **Upgrade notes.** Existing installs: do the SQLite decision above **first**, then **Force Update** in Unraid; `/data` is otherwise left untouched. Fresh installs need no action, they go straight to Postgres as intended.
- **Synapse refused to start (502 Bad Gateway at the reverse proxy) when URL previews were enabled.** The rendered `homeserver-overrides.yaml` set `url_preview_enabled: true` but did **not** include the `url_preview_ip_range_blacklist` that Synapse *requires* whenever URL previews are on. Synapse treats the missing blacklist as a fatal config error and exits on startup, so the homeserver never comes up and the reverse proxy returns `502 Bad Gateway`. This was latent until **v2.0.0**: earlier builds silently ignored the overrides file (the old `include_config_files` approach Synapse never honored), so `url_preview_enabled: true` never actually took effect, and now that the overrides are loaded via `--config-path` the missing blacklist surfaces as a startup crash. The override template now ships the **standard upstream IP blacklist** (SSRF protection, so the link-preview fetcher cannot probe private / internal IP ranges), so URL previews keep working **and** Synapse starts.
- **Upgrade.** **Force Update** the container. `homeserver-overrides.yaml` is regenerated from the template on every start, so the fix applies automatically, with no data changes and no manual editing required. If you need the server up *before* pulling the new image, add the same `url_preview_ip_range_blacklist:` block to `/data/homeserver.yaml` (that file is not regenerated) and restart the container.
